meta.text: Notice the record. With no clustering, the engine has no way to skip files, so it scans all of them and pays full price. Now click the good-order preset, where region comes first and product_id second, and run it again. Watch what happens to the files-scanned number when the leading clustering key matches the filter column. Then try the poor-order preset, where the key order is reversed, and finally the high-cardinality match — a single key with many distinct values that lines up exactly with the filter. As you compare these three, ask yourself: what is the relationship between the leading clustering key, the filter predicate, and the amount of data the query has to read?
